paper_title: Kolmogorov Width of Discrete Linear Spaces: an Approach to Matrix Rigidity
statement: Conjecture 3.7 is such generality. I Remark. Replacing the condition dim(L) ≤ n2+δ in the Conjecture 3.7 by the condition trk(L) ≤ n2+δ makes the Conjecture invalid.
context: Currently it feels that the weakness of our results stems from the fact in that we use relatively little combinatorial structure of F2 -linearity. In particular our strongest result (Theorem 5.5) applies to all sets of bounded triangular rank. Note that while it is plausible that one can make further progress based just on triangular rank; one cannot establish Conjecture 3.7 is such generality. I Remark. Replacing the condition dim(L) ≤ n2+δ in the Conjecture 3.7 by the condition trk(L) ≤ n2+δ makes the Conjecture invalid. Proof. Let m = 1 be an integer. Let Vm0 be a matrix that is obtained from Vm by independently flipping every zero entry to one with probability n−2 . It is not hard to see that with overwhelming probability Vm0 does not contain an all-zeros minor of size Ω(n2 log n). Thus trk(Vm0 ) = O(n2 log n). However Proposition 3.5 implies that for any r = ω(n1− ), we have Ar (Vm0 ) ≈ nr . Thus rows of Vm0 give a counterexample to this stronger version of the Conjecture. J
